primitives.name: File-Based Route Mapping
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Routes TanStack Start uses **file-based routing**. Every `.tsx` file in this directory is a route.
primitives.assumptions: Each .tsx file maps directly to a unique URL path under defined directory structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When new files are added without regeneration of routeTree.gen.ts, typechecking fails.

layer2.mapping: The filesystem hierarchy is isomorphic to the URL namespace, where directory depth corresponds to URL segment nesting.
layer2.telemetry: Route generation success verified by `bun run typecheck`.

primitives.name: Dynamic Path Parameter
primitives.assumptions: Parameterized segments allow runtime variable binding to URL paths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when parameter types mismatch expected schema during runtime.

layer2.mapping: Dynamic parameters derive from static route templates using parameter extraction kernels.
layer2.telemetry: Runtime parameter parsing accuracy validated via route match assertions.

primitives.name: Optional Path Segment
primitives.assumptions: Optional segments enable flexible routing where some path components may be omitted.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Invalidated if required segment is present but format does not match expected pattern.

layer2.mapping: Optional segments are modeled as unary predicates on path component existence within route tree.
layer2.telemetry: Path resolution consistency checked against optional segment presence flags.

The core insight of file-based routing lies in its formal equivalence between directory structures and URL namespaces. This establishes a discrete topological space where each .tsx file represents a point in that space. The bijection ensures deterministic mapping from filesystem to web interface. Dynamic segments introduce parametric variation, allowing continuous deformation of the route manifold while preserving topological integrity. Optional segments extend this by introducing partial functions over the domain of valid paths. Typechecking acts as a constraint satisfaction problem ensuring all possible paths remain well-formed. The failure mode arises when new routes lack regeneration of routeTree.gen.ts, causing divergence between static typing and runtime behavior. This creates a temporal inconsistency in the system's semantic model.
